title: introduce-observability-edge-proxy-and-token-decay-calibrator
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add Observability Edge Proxy to centralize telemetry ingestion and a token-decay-calibrator that reduces warmup-derived noise in token-cost signals; alert tuning to reduce noisy token-cost alerts
description: Motivation: We've seen persistent noisy token-cost alerts correlated with prefix warmups and edge retries in regional proxies. This PR adds an Observability Edge Proxy (OEP) that normalizes metric/tag ingestion (metrics/traces/logs) at the edge and a Token Decay Calibrator (TDC) component that applies a short-lived decay weight to tokens attributable to warmup/retry semantics. Goals: 1) Reduce alert churn by de-emphasizing transient warmup cost spikes; 2) Improve trace/metric coalescing at the edge to lower cardinality and improve downstream rollups; 3) Provide a consistent tag set for downstream dashboards and SLOs. What this changes: - New service: observability/edge-proxy: Go-based sidecar that accepts OTLP/HTTP telemetry, normalizes routing tags (tenant, route, model_variant, region), and emits compacted spans with consistent invocation ids. - New library: telemetry/decay_calibrator: deterministic decay function based on prefix length and retry counts; implemented as a configurable filter in edge-proxy and as a webhook for ingest pipelines. - Dashboard updates: dashboards/token-cost-overview and dashboards/edge-invocations now show pre/post-calibrator series and a decay-adjusted cost band. - Alerts: token-cost long-tail alert rule now uses decay-adjusted aggregation and an adaptive quiet-window (configurable per-tenant). - Tests: unit tests for decay math, integration tests simulating warmup/retry traffic, and e2e for metrics roundtrip. Backwards compatibility: the edge-proxy honors existing tags and can operate in passthrough mode; default decay coefficients match historical baselines, and the feature is gated behind a runtime flag. Rollout plan: canary in a single region for 48h (5% of traffic with decay enabled), metric comparison (pre/post cost percentiles), then ramp to all regions with automatic rollback if token-cost SLO degrades by >5%. Related: ENG-2027 (alert reduction), ENG-2105 (edge telemetry unification).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial edge-proxy scaffold; add OTLP/HTTP normalization pipeline; implement token-decay-calibrator and unit tests; dashboard and alert rule updates; add e2e telemetry smoke tests
review_comments: Priya Sharma: Left small nits in the OTLP normalization code — prefer explicit nil checks and a short comment about tenant fallthrough. Also asked for telemetry metric names to be documented in the README.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed the nil checks and added a short table of metric names and tags to observability/edge-proxy/README.md. Re-ran unit tests.
Marco Gutierrez: Question about decay coefficient defaults — requested an additional integration test that simulates a burst of 200 warmup invocations to verify decay half-life behavior.
Maya Patel (author): Added warmup burst sim in integration-tests and a metric comparison script; left config knobs and added guidance in docs/observability/token-decay.md.
Hana Kim: Suggested alert threshold tuning and requested a smoke test for the adaptive quiet-window to ensure it doesn't mute genuine regressions. Approved after CI passed.
post_merge_notes: Canary started 2026-03-02 in us-west-2 with 5% traffic. Early signal: 22% reduction in 95th token-cost spikes attributable to warmup; a follow-up PR will tune decay coefficients per-tenant based on machine-learning fit. Monitoring: added grafana panel and a synthetic compare job.
